title: Cap. V Obj. 4 Sol: eternal will to save ≠ all that concurs in the consummated external act
pass_a_gloss: Solution. I answer, That not all those things concur unto the eternal will of saving enclosed in the secret purpose of election, which concur unto the will of saving consummated in the very external act. We therefore deny the consequence of the Major, and say that God never had a will of saving anyone without satisfaction of his justice; yet had a will of giving certain ones to Christ, of giving them faith by which this union would be made, and by which, with this faith mediating, he would efficaciously be satisfied for them through the death of Christ: and all these things antecedently to the foresight of faith as certainly and infallibly existing in them; yet not without foresight, or by excluding the foresight of faith to be infallibly imparted to them from the grace of God.
pass_b_english: Sol. I answer: not everything that concurs in the will to save as consummated in the external act also concurs in the eternal will to save enclosed in election's secret purpose. We deny the Major's consequence. God never had a will to save anyone without satisfaction of his justice; yet he had a will to give certain ones to Christ, to give them faith by which that union would be made, and by which, with that faith mediating, he would be efficaciously satisfied for them through Christ's death — all of this antecedent to foresight of faith as already certainly and infallibly existing in them, yet not without foresight, nor by excluding foresight of faith to be infallibly imparted to them from God's grace.
source_text: Sol. Respondeo, Non concurrere ad voluntatem aeternam servandi in arcano electionis proposito inclusam, illa omnia quae concurrunt ad voluntatem servandi in ipso actu externo consummatam. Negamus igitur Majoris consequentiam, atque dicimus, Deum nunquam habuisse voluntatem servandi quenquam absque satisfactione justitiae suae; habuisse tamen voluntatem dandi quosdam Christo, dandi illis fidem per quam unio haec fieret, et per quam mediante hac fide Deo pro illis per Christi mortem efficaciter satisfaceret: atque haec omnia antecedenter ad praevisionem fidei ut in illis certe et infallibiliter existentis; non tamen absque praevisione, aut excludendo praevisionem fidei illis ex gratia Dei infallibiliter impertiendae.
